text:
emma: quick thread: i want to float a remap-first migration idea for pinned/host-backed pages to reduce copy cost during cross-node/NUMA tenant shifts. sketch below.

ryan: remap-first sounds sweet for latency, but what kernel primitives are you expecting to use? mremap/switch_pmd? cuda-pinned pages complicate this.

emma: agreed, CUDA device memory is out-of-scope — we only target host-backed, potentially mlocked or pinned pages we already use for KV and staging. plan is: try kernel-assisted page migration (migrate_pages) or remap trick to move the mapping/ownership without an explicit user-land memcpy. if those fail, fall back to an async copy path.

lulu: migrate_pages requires privileges and isn't always available in containers. also migrating mlocked pages can be racy with TLBs and device DMA. we should enumerate failure modes up front.

emma: yes. i propose a 3-tier strategy: 
  1) fast-remap: if page is anonymous host-backed and kernel supports move without unpin (same machine), attempt remap/migrate_pages and claim success if syscall returns 0.
  2) helper-daemon: if syscall needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN, send a signed request to a privileged local agent that performs the migrate on behalf of runtime. agent enforces tenant ACLs.
  3) copy-fallback: if migrate not supported or fails, create a shared shm segment on the target NUMA node and copy in the background (rate-limited). once copied, atomically switch pointers.

charlie: atomic switch pointers across threads/processes is tricky. do we plan to use a small indirection table so we can update the mapping atomically and invalidate per-thread caches?

emma: yes — allocator will use an indirection layer: small metadata word per slab that maps logical -> physical. switch is CAS on metadata. runtime threads consult metadata before deref. we already do similar for slab relocating for compaction.

zhi: what's the expected perf delta? copying K MB at 10GB/s vs migrate cost & latency? also circuit-breakers for thrash?

emma: on local NUMA tests: migrating ~32MB slab via migrate_pages completed ~3x faster than user-land memcpy (measured wall time under controlled test). fallback copy has higher CPU cost but is rate-limited to avoid thrash. we'll add a `migrate_rate_limit_mb_s` per-tenant and a `migrate_hysteresis_ms` to avoid repeated moves.

ryan: security & correctness concerns: pinned pages used by kvcache may have outstanding references. we must ensure no outstanding DMA or device mapping. how do we check?

emma: reclaimer/coordinator will check refcounts and a small `inflight_ops` bit. we only remap when refcount==0 and no pinned dma-buf handles. if a page is pinned by kernel for DMA, the migrate syscall should fail; treat that as `DEFER`.

lulu: also remember pinned pages require unpin (munlock) to free; unpin is expensive. if remap avoids unpin, great. we should instrument unpin latency.

charlie: propose runtime API and return codes so higher layers can react:
```c
enum migrate_result { MIG_OK, MIG_DEFER, MIG_COPY_FAILED };
int try_migrate(void *addr, size_t len, int flags);
```
where flags include `MIG_FORCE_COPY`, `MIG_NO_PRIV_HELPER`.

emma: exact proto in the runtime will be: `migrate_async(addr,len,opts)->migration_id` and a callback or pollable status (ok|deferred|failed). synchronous `try_migrate()` will be convenience wrapper.

ryan: instrumentation ideas: counters for `migrate_attempts`, `migrate_success_remap`, `migrate_success_helper`, `migrate_fallback_copy`, `migrate_deferred_refcount`, and histograms for `migrate_latency` and `unpin_latency`. alert if fallback_copy ratio > 0.1 or migrate_latency_p95 > 500ms.

emma: agreed. we'll expose per-tenant gauges. ops can set thresholds.

ops-bot: note: privileged helper daemon will require a security review + packaging. add to canary checklist.

lulu: rollout: opt-in per-tenant with `migrate_strategy: remap|helper|copy`. default `copy` for now. schedule: dev canary -> internal small fleet -> region canary.

emma: config example: 
```yaml
runtime:
  migrate:
    enabled: true
    default_strategy: remap
    migrate_rate_limit_mb_s: 32
    migrate_hysteresis_ms: 10000
    privileged_helper_socket: /var/run/infra/migrate.sock
```

charlie: edge cases: kernels that report success but silently stall TLB shootdown for long periods. add a safety timeout: if remap-in-progress > X seconds, mark slab as suspect and copy as rescue. also add a monotonic `migrate_version` on slab metadata to detect partial updates.

zhi: cross-host vs cross-numa: cross-host remap impossible; we'll only do network RDMA/direct copy for cross-host. make sure control plane picks correct strategy per-deployment.

emma: good point. runtime will detect `same_host` vs `cross_host` and pick available ops.

ryan: tests: fuzz remap with simulated refcount races; run with heap-fuzzer + our device emulator for 72h on canary nodes. also inject migrate_pages failures to exercise fallback.

ops-bot: checklist added: security review, helper-daemon packaging, metrics, per-tenant flag, grafana panel, rollout playbook. see /deploy/migrate-remap.

emma: i'll open a follow-up RFC with the syscall matrix, helper protocol, protobuf for helper requests, and a small PoC daemon. putting perf numbers & test harness in that PR.

devops-bot: created INF-5003 migrate-remap helper + label `mem-migrate`

charlie: ack. one more ask: please record a short demo script that toggles `migrate_strategy` per-tenant and dumps `migrate_*` metrics. will help ops run the A/B.

emma: will attach scripts and initial grafana mock in the RFC. thanks all :eyes:
